title: Linked lists using objects
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: What does a partition do to the pivot?
questions.answer: Places it at its final index with smaller/equal values to its left.
options: Places it at its final index with greater/equal values to its left.
Places it at its final index with smaller/equal values to its left.
Places it at its final index with smaller/equal values to its right.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Places it at its final index with smaller/equal values to its left.

questions.prompt: What does the head reference identify?
questions.answer: The first node in a linked list.
options: The first node in a linked list.
The first node in a linked record.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: The first node in a linked list.

questions.prompt: Why must a new node's Next be set before replacing an existing Next link?
questions.answer: Otherwise the original successor can become unreachable and part of the list may be lost.
options: Otherwise the original successor can become unreachable OR part of the list may be lost.
Otherwise the original successor can become unreachable and part of the record may be lost.
Otherwise the original successor can become unreachable and part of the list may be lost.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Otherwise the original successor can become unreachable and part of the list may be lost.
